newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas little changed in choppy trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas little changed in choppy trade.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were little changed Tuesday despite some early volatility in response to the wavering futures market, market sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices slipped two cents to the high-$1.80s per mmBtu, with Henry Hub quoted mostly in the low-$1.90s.
In south Texas, however, prices edged up two cents to the mid-$1.80s as storage buying continued in the producing region.
"Everyone tried to take it much lower, but it just never really happened," one trader said.
Early in the NYMEX session, April Henry Hub natgas futures drifted lower into the high-$1.80s, then rebounded to a high of $1.95. As of 1336 EST, the contract was 4.2 cents lower at $1.895.
In the East, New York city-gate prices were mostly steady in the low-$2.20s, supported by cooler-than-normal weather in the region.
In the Midcontinent, prices were up one cent to the mid-$1.70s to low-$1.80s, with Demarcation quoted mostly in the mid-to-high $1.70s.
Temperatures in the Midwest are expected to run near to slightly above normal through the end of the week.
In the Permian basin, gas prices fell three cents to the mid-$1.70s as temperatures in the state hovered near normal.
Southern California border prices were similarly lower in the high-$1.70s to mid-$1.80s.
The restart of the 1,070 megawatt San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in southern California will likely be delayed again to a new date of March 20 following repairs of a leak, Edison International said.
Withdrawal estimates for American Gas Association's storage report on Wednesday range from 30 to 85 bcf, compared with 118 bcf a year ago.
